name: Battle of Lepanto
note: The Holy League fleet formed in a north-south line, the Ottoman fleet facing it from the east. The galleasses are drawn as one block; the accounts do not say which Turkish galleys they fired on. They give no distances, so the gaps between formations are only a guide.

terrain.name: Northern shore of the Gulf
terrain.quote: close to the northern shore of the Gulf

units.name: Holy League left division
units.quote: Left Division of 53 galleys (mainly Venetian) and 2 galleasses, led by Agostino Barbarigo

units.name: Holy League centre division
units.quote: The Centre Division consisted of 62 galleys (and 2 galleasses) under John of Austria himself in his galley La Real

units.name: Holy League right division
units.quote: The Right Division to the south consisted of another 53 galleys (and 2 galleasses) under the Genoese Giovanni Andrea Doria

units.name: Holy League reserve
units.quote: A reserve division of 38 galleys was stationed behind (that is, to the west of) the main fleet

units.name: Galleasses
units.quote: Four galeasses stationed in front of the Christian battle line opened fire at close quarters at the foremost Turkish galleys

units.name: Ottoman right
units.quote: 54 galleys and two galliots on its right under Mehmed Siroco.

units.name: Ottoman centre
units.quote: 88 galleys and eight galliots in the centre under Ali Pasha in the Sultana.

units.name: Ottoman left
units.quote: 61 galleys and 32 galliots in the south offshore under Uluç Ali.

phases.title: The two fleets draw up in line
phases.text: The Holy League fleet formed four divisions in a north-south line, its left towards the coast. The Ottoman fleet faced it with a right, a centre and a left under Uluç Ali offshore in the south.
phases.quote: the Christian fleet formed up in four divisions in a north–south line

phases.title: The galleasses open fire
phases.text: The wind shifted to favour the Christians shortly before contact. Galleasses in front of their line fired at close quarters at the foremost Turkish galleys and confused their battle array.
phases.quote: Four galeasses stationed in front of the Christian battle line opened fire at close quarters at the foremost Turkish galleys, confusing their battle array in the crucial moment of contact.

phases.title: Barbarigo and Sirocco meet by the shore
phases.text: First contact was between Barbarigo and Sirocco near the northern shore. Barbarigo tried to keep close to the coast, but Sirocco knew the depth of the water and put galleys between his line and the shore. The ships closed into a hand-to-hand melee.
phases.quote: Sirocco, knowing the depth of the waters, managed to still insert galleys between Barbarigo's line and the coast.

phases.title: Barbarigo is killed and Bazán's reserve arrives
phases.text: Barbarigo was killed by an arrow to the eye. The timely arrival of Bazán with the reserve fleet balanced the situation on the left.
phases.quote: Barbarigo was killed by an arrow to the eye, but the timely arrival of Bazán with the reserve fleet balanced the situation

phases.title: Sirocco is killed and the freed slaves join in
phases.text: Sirocco was eventually killed and beheaded. Christian galley slaves freed from the Turkish ships were given arms and joined the fighting, which turned the battle on this wing in the Christian favour.
phases.quote: The Christian galley slaves freed from the Turkish ships were supplied with arms and joined in the fighting, turning the battle in favour of the Christian side.

phases.title: The centres clash around the flagships
phases.text: The centres met so hard that Ali Pasha's galley drove into the Real as far as the fourth rowing bench. Spanish Tercio infantry and Turkish janissaries fought hand to hand around the two flagships.
phases.quote: the centres clashed with such force that Ali Pasha's galley drove into the Real as far as the fourth rowing bench

phases.title: Colonna's counter-attack clears the Real
phases.text: When the Real was nearly taken, Colonna came alongside with the bow of his galley and mounted a counter-attack. With his help the Turks were pushed off the Real.
phases.quote: When the Real was nearly taken, Colonna came alongside, with the bow of his galley, and mounted a counter-attack.

phases.title: The Turkish flagship is taken
phases.text: The Turkish flagship was boarded and swept, and its whole crew was killed, Ali Pasha among them. After two hours of fighting the Turks were beaten on the left and in the centre.
phases.quote: The flagship's entire crew was killed, including Ali Pasha himself.

phases.title: Doria sails south and opens a gap
phases.text: On the Christian right Doria went on sailing south instead of taking his assigned position, and opened a wide gap with the centre. His captains took his signals for treachery.
phases.quote: Doria continued sailing towards the south instead of taking his assigned position.

phases.title: Uluç Ali turns on the centre
phases.text: With Doria too far away to interfere, Uluç Ali swung round and fell on Colonna's southern flank. He attacked some fifteen galleys round the flagship of the Knights of Malta.
phases.quote: Uluç Ali swung around and fell on Colonna's southern flank, with Doria too far away to interfere.

phases.title: Bazán's reserve arrives and Uluç Ali retreats
phases.text: The arrival of the reserve under Bazán kept Uluç Ali from breaking into the Christian centre. He was forced to retreat and escaped the battle with the captured flag of the Knights of Malta.
phases.quote: This was prevented again by the arrival of the reserve squadron commanded by Bazán. Uluç Ali was forced to retreat
